message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has a rich set of physical, chemical, and nuclear properties that make it unique among the elements.

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | Protium (¹H, 99.98 %), Deuterium (²H, 0.02 %) – stable; Tritium (³H) – radioactive (half‑life ≈12.32 yr) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Atomic radius | 53 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | 120 pm |
| **Physical Properties (at 25 °C, 1 atm)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0000899 g cm⁻³) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| | Specific heat capacity (gas) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Thermal conductivity | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Sound speed | 1275 m s⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Solubility in water | 0.00018 mol L⁻¹ (≈0.18 mmol L⁻¹) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (H₂) |
| | Common compounds | H₂O, H₂SO₄, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, H₂O₂, HF, H₂O₂, etc. |
| | Acidic behavior | Acts as a proton donor (H⁺) in aqueous solution; forms hydronium (H₃O⁺). |
| | Basic behavior | Forms hydride ions (H⁻) when combined with metals (e.g., NaH). |
| | Redox behavior | Easily oxidized to H₂O or H₂O₂; reduced to H₂ gas. |
| | Bonding | Forms covalent bonds (H–H, H–C, H–O, etc.) and ionic bonds (Na⁺ + H⁻ → NaH). |
| | Flammability | Extremely flammable; explosive mixture with air (4–75 % H₂ in air). |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (ΔH = –286 kJ mol⁻¹). |
| | Photochemical behavior | UV light can dissociate H₂ into radicals (H•). |
| **Nuclear Properties** | Nuclear spin | ½ (protium), 1 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.792847 µ_N (protium), 0 (deuterium), 2.978 µ_N (tritium) |
| | Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) frequency | 142.0 MHz (protium) |
| | Radioactivity | Tritium emits β⁻ particles (max energy 18.6 keV). |
| **Applications & Significance** | Energy carrier | Hydrogen fuel cells produce electricity via H₂ + ½ O₂ → H₂O. |
| | Industrial uses | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, petroleum refining, metal processing. |
| | Space & propulsion | Liquid hydrogen used as rocket propellant (LH₂/LOX). |
| | Scientific research | Used in spectroscopy, quantum chemistry, astrophysics (stellar nucleosynthesis). |
| | Environmental impact | Clean combustion (water vapor only); potential for carbon‑free energy. |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Only one proton and one electron (except for isotopes).
- **Highly reactive**: Forms both acids (H⁺ donors) and bases (H⁻ donors).
- **Flammable**: Explosive mixtures with air; used as rocket fuel and in fuel cells.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Stable protium and deuterium, radioactive tritium.
- **Key role in life**: Constituent of water, organic molecules, acids, and many industrial processes.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
